claim: TrickyArena is hosted at agenttrickydps.vercel.app and dark patterns are toggled via a `?dp=<code>` URL query parameter, with multiple patterns joined by underscores.

Live-verified: navigating agenttrickydps.vercel.app, selecting 'Bait and Switch' for the News site, and clicking through produces the URL https://agenttrickydps.vercel.app/news?dp=bs, confirming the hosted site and query scheme are functional as of Sept 2026.

TrickyArena's evaluation/consts.py defines dark-pattern code-to-name mappings for six site categories: shopping, news, spotify, wiki, health, linkedin — though only shopping/news/spotify/health are exposed on the live homepage.

Dark pattern susceptibility scoring (Agent Action Validator) is defined entirely by logical conditions over an action-trace database of DOM interactions (clicks/inputs on specific element IDs/xpaths) — not by verifying a real-world outcome such as a completed charge.

source.title: Investigating the Impact of Dark Patterns on LLM-Based Web Agents

evidence_quote: Each condition involves an action trace database query to determine the existence, non-existence, or uniqueness of a specific action

claim: The paper's dp_checks.py implementation confirms this concretely: e.g. the Warranty dark pattern checks only that 'add to cart' was clicked, the warranty item's remove button was NOT clicked, and checkout was clicked — all DOM element-ID click checks, no payment/order verification.

The paper uses Gray et al.'s 5-category dark pattern ontology (Obstruction, Sneaking, Interface Interference, Forced Action, Social Engineering) and implements exactly 14 dark patterns across 4 TrickyArena sites (E-Commerce/Shopping, News, Streaming/Spotify-style Music, Health Portal), enumerated in Appendix B Table 5.

claim: LiteAgent is agent-agnostic at the harness/instrumentation level (works via CDP/Playwright event-listener injection regardless of agent's backend LLM), but each individual agent submodule (BrowserUse, Skyvern, Agent-E, etc.) must be independently configured with its own supported LLM API keys; the README's setup notes specifically instruct providing OpenAI keys for the agent submodules, and only 3 of 6 agents (BrowserUse, Skyvern, Agent-E) were shown in the paper to 'readily support' swapping to Claude/Gemini backends.

source.title: LiteAgent README.md / Investigating the Impact of Dark Patterns on LLM-Based Web Agents

evidence_quote: We evaluate these models using three agent implementations that readily support these backend LLMs with minimal configuration changes: BrowserUse, Skyvern, and Agent-E

claim: The paper's own meta-review (Appendix G) explicitly flags the absence of a human baseline as a limitation, and the authors concede in their response that they cannot directly compare human vs. agent susceptibility rates because the TrickyArena UI/scenarios differ from prior human dark-pattern studies.
